ledger.claim: POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess of actual over optimal distance exceeds both 20% of the optimal distance and 0.8 km in absolute terms. Here the trace covers 3.4 km against a 6.4 km optimal route, an excess of -3.0 km (derived excess_pct -46.875%): the vehicle drove less far than the optimal route, so neither establishment test can pass and no deviation exists. Under POL-RD-01 the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement where it differs from the rounded trip_record convenience copy, and the trace-derived deviation status is expressly 'no deviation'. There is no admissible measurement in this bundle on which the rider can clear the POL-RD-01 threshold.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from a gps_trace that is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c). The trace is unimpaired - 100% coverage, 55 fixes at a 10 s cadence, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 s - yet it discloses no excess at all. The burden is never discharged and the driver is never put to an exculpatory clause.

This trip is UPFRONT_QUOTE with a quoted_fare_sgd of 7.20, so under POL-RD-11 the POL-RD-02 distance-and-time recomputation does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however the trip is characterised. The only route-deviation remedy is the POL-RD-11(a) amount by which charged_total exceeds the quote: charged_total is SGD 7.20, the quoted fare is SGD 7.20, and the properly chargeable pass-through and statutory lines total SGD 0.00, so the remedy computes to SGD 0.00.

Nothing in the fare engages the POL-RD-09 pass-through and billing-integrity corrections: there are no ERP gantry lines (total SGD 0.00), no airport surcharge - the trip ends at a shelter and does not originate at an airport - and a waiting-time fee of SGD 0.00. With no off-route or phantom line, POL-RD-09(4) is not triggered and no standalone refund or billing-integrity referral arises.

The only chat message is the driver's own note that he would end the trip; it records no rider instruction and no departure from the optimal corridor. It describes a trip cut short, which the trace corroborates - 3.4 km driven against a 6.4 km optimal route - and route deviation provides no refund for a trip driven under its optimal distance. The message changes none of the arithmetic under POL-RD-01 or POL-RD-11.

Even if POL-RD-06 were consulted, no repeat-deviation pattern is established: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250, below both the count-of-three gate and the 0.05 ratio gate. POL-RD-06 is in any event not triggered, because no material deviation is recorded on this trip.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver: I have decided this case on the route-deviation policy, which is the category it was filed under, and every figure below is read off the record so both of you can check it.

The governing measurement is the GPS trace. EV-GPS-00715 is unimpaired — 100% coverage, 55 fixes at the published 10-second cadence, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 s — so no POL-RD-07 issue arises and nothing has to be reconstructed across a gap. The trace shows the vehicle covered 3.4 km (trace_distance_km) against a booked optimal route of 6.4 km (trip_record.optimal_distance_km). The excess is 3.4 − 6.4 = −3.0 km, i.e. −46.9%. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess is greater than 20% of the optimal distance and greater than 0.8 km; a negative excess fails both tests, so no deviation exists and the clause directs NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised.

That closes the distance-and-time route. This was an upfront-quoted trip (fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE on EV-FARE-00715), so POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available. The only route-deviation money is the POL-RD-11(a) amount by which charged_total exceeds the quote plus the properly chargeable pass-through and statutory lines. Charged_total is SGD 7.20, quoted_fare_sgd is SGD 7.20, and there are no ERP gantry lines (SGD 0.00), no airport surcharge, and a waiting-time fee of SGD 0.00, so that amount computes to SGD 0.00 — the fare artifact itself publishes pol_rd_11_remedy 0.00. I have also checked POL-RD-09: with no charge line the trace never crossed and no surcharge on a trip that does not originate at an airport, there is no billing-integrity correction and no POL-RD-09(4) referral.

The rider's account of what happened is not in dispute and I accept it. The driver's own in-app message at 12:25:40, "Hospital too far in this jam. I will end here and refund you.", and the trip record's dropoff label, "Shelter where service ended", show the trip was ended short of the hospital. But no clause in this policy turns an unfinished trip into a refund: the route-deviation clauses measure excess over the optimal route, not distance left undriven, and the upfront rules fix the fare at booking and close the distance-and-time route. The driver's "in this jam" explanation does him no good either — the only traffic advisory for the trip, EV-ADVIS-00715-01, is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run on this record and, per POL-RD-13, an uncited traffic assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Nothing here decides against the rider's honesty; the route-deviation rules simply provide no money for these facts.

No clause in this policy produces a referral, and no POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires: the trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, the trace is unimpaired, no timestamps conflict, no exculpatory clause has been invoked against a cited artifact, and no charge line lacks a counterpart. The disputed SGD 7.20 therefore stands as charged: fare_breakdown.payment_status (CHARGED) and refund_issued_sgd (0.00) are left as they are.

One open question, which belongs here rather than in any referral: the record shows you were carried 3.4 km of a 6.4 km journey and charged the full upfront fare of SGD 7.20, and the driver told you in writing that a refund was coming. That may well be worth pursuing, but it is not a route deviation and this policy gives me no power over it. If you wish to take it further, raise it directly with support as a trip-completion or service dispute.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
